title: Integral exchange after base change to a geometric point
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. For any Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with horizontal maps $g':X'\to X$ and $s$ and vertical maps $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $f$, the canonical exchange component [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $s^* f_*F\to f'_*g'^*F$ is an isomorphism. No torsion, finite-type, surjectivity or residue-field algebraicity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EYP (integral direct-image base change); strict-henselian proof via Tags 03Q9, 09XK, 09ZH and 0A3I

proof.text: Apply the integral geometric fibre section theorem to obtain an invertible module map Theta with its formula on every neighbourhood germ.

Apply the general geometric fibre exchange germ identity to Theta. Its target comparison b and the inverse-image source comparison a are isomorphisms, so the identity stalk of the actual exchange is an isomorphism by cancellation of b.

The identity geometric point covers Spec Omega. The universe-lifted family consisting of this point is conservative. Transport the identity stalk through uliftSheafFiberIso and apply the conservative-family criterion.
